_comment: Provenance for the programs beside this file: what create_item("0180", <the prompt `run.ts prompts` printed>) returned. `language` is what the PLATFORM routed the request to, which is not always what was asked for — see c1-t9-tm5-shorttext.

c1-t9-tm5-shorttext.note: Asked for 0180, and it has never routed correctly. On 2026-09-04 the composer re-routed it to 0175 and returned a claims-and-evidence program (kept beside this file as the evidence). Retested 2026-09-05 after the catalog was updated: it now STAYS on 0180 and is refused at the scope gate instead, with a message that contradicts itself — "This request doesn't fit any available Graffiticode language. This is a written-response assessment item with a rubric for hand-scoring, which is explicitly in scope for L0180's extended-text interaction type." The verdict and its own rationale disagree, so the gate is voting against what it just described. The failure changed shape rather than being fixed; it is a console routing problem either way, not an expressiveness gap — conformance.test.ts scores this shape as an extended-text and port.ts builds it mechanically.
